Preparing for the future and key growth moves
nodes.summary: Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories is a global pharmaceutical company committed to affordable and innovative medicines, with a portfolio spanning APIs, generics, biosimilars, OTC, and custom services across key therapeutic areas. The document outlines its purpose, values, and leadership behaviors. FY2025 highlights include double-digit growth across all markets, EBITDA margin of 28.3%, and ROCE of ~28%. Strategic moves include acquisitions (Nicotinell), partnerships (Nestle, Gilead), and in-licensing (Vonoprazan, Toripalimab). Innovation efforts feature a biologics CDMO facility and oncology assets. Quality compliance and sustainability achievements are noted (68% renewable power, 60% carbon neutral, MSCI upgrade). The message also addresses future challenges, including anticipated U.S. product competition in 2026, and outlines strategies for continued growth.

nodes.title: OUR STRATEGY PILLARS
nodes.summary: The text outlines a pharmaceutical company's strategy centered on three pillars: leadership in chosen spaces, operational excellence and continuous improvement, and patient-centric product innovation, all guided by the purpose 'Good Health Can't Wait' and principles of empathy and dynamism. It details leadership efforts to accelerate access to affordable medicines, develop complex products, and expand market presence. Core business areas include global generics (branded and unbranded), biosimilars, and pharmaceutical services and active ingredients (PSAI), with major markets such as the USA, India, Russia & CIS, China, Brazil, South Africa, and Europe. Future growth investments cover access to novel molecules, CAR-T capabilities via Aurigene Oncology, and consumer health expansion. Operational excellence uses Lean Management System to boost productivity, while patient-centric innovation focuses on differentiated products, new technologies, AI/ML, and partnerships.

The OpsNext programme, a digital lighthouse, implemented over 40 Industry 4.0 initiatives using advanced analytics, digital twins, RPA, AR/VR/MR, digital performance management, and IIoT, expanding in FY2025 with smart investigator, golden tunnel, and manufacturing schedulers. Key achievements: AI platform adoption in three business units (~US$1.75 mn value across ~40 molecules), 230+ golden tunnels impacting 300+ critical quality attributes, manufacturing scheduler enabling touchless scheduling, and smart investigator reducing data collation time by ~80%. nodes.title: Impairment, Employee Benefits, and Share-Based Payment Accounting Policies
nodes.summary: The page covers impairment testing principles including annual testing for goodwill and indefinite-lived intangibles, recoverable amount determination via value in use or fair value less costs to sell, cash-generating unit allocation, loss recognition, and reversal rules for goodwill, other assets, joint ventures, and equity-accounted investees. It also details employee benefits: short-term benefits expensed as incurred with liability recognition, defined contribution plan charges, defined benefit obligations actuarially calculated using projected unit credit method with service costs in profit or loss and actuarial gains/losses in OCI, other long-term benefits discounted and recognized in profit or loss, and compensated absences measured actuarially. Finally, it covers share-based payments: equity-settled options measured at grant-date fair value using Black-Scholes-Merton, expensed over vesting with adjustments for expected vesting, and cash-settled transactions expensed with liability remeasurement at each reporting and settlement date.

nodes.title: m) Provisions
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for provisions, including recognition, discounting, and onerous contracts; contingent liabilities and assets; and revenue recognition. Revenue topics include sale of goods (generic products in India, APIs and intermediates, exports), profit share revenues, out-licensing arrangements, milestone payments, royalties, and provisions for chargebacks, rebates, discounts, and shelf stock adjustments. It details recognition points, measurement of transaction price, variable consideration, and specific arrangements with business partners.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: Provisions, Contingencies, Revenue Recognition and Related Estimates
key_items: Out licensing arrangements, milestone payments and royalties
Provision for chargeback, rebates and discounts
nodes.summary: The page covers accounting policies for onerous contracts (provision recognition and measurement), contingent liabilities and assets (disclosure and recognition criteria), and revenue recognition. Revenue sections address sale of goods (control transfer, transaction price, variable consideration), profit share revenues (base price and profit share recognition), out-licensing arrangements including milestone payments and royalties (upfront fees, performance obligations, deferrals), provisions for chargeback, rebates and discounts (estimation based on contractual terms, historical data, and judgments), and shelf stock adjustments (credits for price decreases). Throughout, the text emphasizes estimation, judgment, and timing of recognition.

nodes.title: Shelf stock adjustments
nodes.summary: This text outlines accounting policies from the notes to consolidated financial statements (FY 2024-25, Indian Rupees millions). It covers provisions for onerous contracts (measured at present value of lower of termination or net continuing cost, with prior impairment of related assets) and contingent liabilities/assets (disclosure thresholds; no recognition of contingent assets unless virtually certain). Revenue recognition policies include: sales of goods (control transfer timing, transaction price net of returns/taxes/discounts, variable consideration constraint, principal vs. agent); specific timing for domestic generic products, APIs/intermediates, exports; profit-share arrangements (base price on delivery, additional profit share when highly probable); out-licensing, milestone payments, royalties (upfront fees deferred if performance obligations remain, milestones recognized upon achievement, royalty income when underlying sales occur); provisions for chargebacks, rebates, discounts, Medicaid; shelf stock adjustments; refund liabilities and return assets; service revenue (contract research recognized as performed, upfront payments deferred); license fees; shipping and handling costs as other expenses. Also covers other income and finance costs (interest income via effective interest method, dividend income when right established, borrowing costs expensed unless capitalized, foreign exchange gains/losses net in other income/expense). Finally, income tax accounting (current and deferred tax, recognition exceptions, measurement, offsetting, and accruals for uncertain tax positions).

nodes.title: Accounting Policies for Revenue, Refunds, Services, Licensing, and Finance Costs
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for sales returns and refund liabilities, including shelf stock adjustments based on historical experience and contract terms, with corresponding assets for returned goods. It covers revenue recognition for services (contract research, upfront payments deferred), license fees (recognized on control transfer and performance obligation completion), and shipping and handling costs (expensed as other expenses). Other income (interest, dividends, gains on financial assets) and finance costs (interest on borrowings, recognized using effective interest method unless capitalized) are detailed, including classification of associated cash flows and net reporting of foreign currency gains/losses.

nodes.title: q) Income tax
nodes.summary: The text covers income tax accounting, including current and deferred tax recognition, exceptions for deferred tax, deferred tax assets, measurement, offsetting, and uncertain tax positions, plus the OECD Pillar Two exception. It also addresses government grants, segment reporting, dividend recognition, rounding of amounts, and fair value determination. Fair value section includes hierarchy levels, valuation methods for intangible assets, inventories, investments, derivatives, non-derivative financial liabilities, contingent consideration, and involvement of external valuers.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: Tax, Grants, Segments, Dividends, Fair Value
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies including tax uncertainty and OECD Pillar Two exception, government grants recognition, segment reporting to the chief operating decision maker, dividend liability timing, and rounding of amounts. It details fair value determination methods, hierarchy levels (1-3), and valuation approaches for intangible assets, inventories, investments, derivatives, non-derivative financial liabilities, and contingent consideration, including use of external valuers and recurring fair value transfers.

nodes.title: Fair Value Measurement Policies and Methods
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for income tax uncertainty, OECD Pillar Two exception, government grants, segment reporting, dividend recognition, and rounding. It details fair value determination: definition, market assumptions, and hierarchy levels (1-3). It explains valuation methods for intangible assets using multi-period excess earnings, inventories based on selling price less costs and profit margin, equity/debt securities and mutual funds using quoted prices or discounted cash flows, derivatives using discounted forward price differences or appropriate techniques, and non-derivative financial liabilities using present value of cash flows at market interest rates.

It then details product and patent matters related to the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority, specifically the Norfloxacin litigation in India: the 1995 NPPA designation and price fixation, the Company's 1996 writ petition, the High Court's dismissal in 2004, the Supreme Court appeal, the 2006 NPPA recovery notice, the Company's writ petition and partial deposits, the 2013 Supreme Court writ petition, the 2016 remand to the High Court, and the 2016 dismissal of the Special Leave Petition on price fixing. It notes similar writ petitions for Theophylline/Doxofylline, Cloxacillin, and Ciprofloxacin, consolidated and adjourned to July 29, 2025. The Company has recorded a provision for potential liability for excess sale proceeds and interest, and believes further liability from penalties is not probable.

It also covers the ranitidine recall and litigation: the voluntary recall due to NDMA, the federal MDL 2924 with over 3,275 lawsuits, dismissals based on federal preemption, ongoing appeals, and state court actions including New Mexico, Baltimore, California Proposition 65, and Illinois consolidated cases. nodes.summary: The text covers two contingent liability matters. First, a legal dispute with the NPPA over a demand notice for excess sale proceeds, including the company's writ petition, stay, provision of ₹479 million, and the matter adjourned to July 2025. Second, the ranitidine recall and federal MDL 2924 litigation: the voluntary recall due to NDMA, establishment of MDL 2924 with over 3,275 lawsuits, dismissal of generic manufacturer claims based on federal preemption, appeals to the 11th Circuit, summary judgments for brand defendants on designated cancers, and the status of appeals with oral argument scheduled for July 2025.

nodes.title: State Court Ranitidine-related Actions
nodes.summary: The text describes state court ranitidine litigation involving the Company. New Mexico's AG filed a public nuisance and negligence suit; a preemption motion to dismiss was denied, and trial is scheduled for September 2025 with a continuance requested. Baltimore's similar suit was dismissed with prejudice on preemption. A California Proposition 65 case was dismissed on demurrer, affirmed on appeal, and review denied. Over 360 plaintiffs filed failure-to-warn, design-defect, and negligence claims across five states; the Company was dismissed from New Jersey, New York, and Pennsylvania cases. Illinois consolidated cases were dismissed with prejudice on preemption, with appeals pending in Valadez and an interlocutory appeal. California cases were transferred to a JCCP, where some claims proceeded, and a confidential master settlement was executed in December 2024. The Company denies wrongdoing, intends to defend vigorously, and states liability is unascertainable, so no provision was made.

nodes.title: Class Action under the Canadian Competition Act filed in Federal Court in Toronto, Canada
nodes.summary: The text describes two legal proceedings: a Canadian class action under the Competition Act alleging an industry-wide conspiracy to allocate markets, fix prices, and maintain supply of generic drugs, with multiple amended claims and a certification motion scheduled for October 2025; and U.S. antitrust multi-district litigation (MDL 2724) involving approximately 250 plaintiffs and 206 cases, alleging a conspiracy among generic drug manufacturers to fix prices, allocate markets, and engage in bid rigging, with claims brought by state attorneys general, direct purchasers, indirect resellers, end payers, and individual direct action plaintiffs. The Company is named as a defendant in both proceedings, denies the allegations, intends to defend vigorously, and states that any liability is unascertainable, so no provision has been made in the financial statements.

nodes.title: Civil litigation with Mezzion
nodes.summary: Mezzion Pharma and Mezzion International filed a complaint in January 2017 in New Jersey Superior Court against the Company and its U.S. subsidiary regarding production and supply of udenafil API and finished dosage from 2007-2015. Mezzion alleges failure to comply with U.S. FDA cGMP, causing delay in NDA filing. The Company filed a motion to dismiss for lack of jurisdiction, denied in January 2018; interlocutory appeal denied. Case is in pretrial discovery. The Company denies wrongdoing, intends to defend vigorously, and states liability is unascertainable, so no provision was made in the financial statements.

nodes.title: Revlimid® Antitrust Litigation
nodes.summary: The text details antitrust litigation involving Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories (DRL) over Revlimid® and generics. Since 2019, In re Revlimid action has been pending against Celgene, BMS, and later Teva and Natco. In 2023–2024, Hospital Plaintiffs (Mayo Clinic, LifePoint, Intermountain Health) and Retailer Plaintiffs (Walgreens, Kroger, CVS) sued DRL, and United, Insurer Plaintiffs, and EPP Plaintiffs added DRL to existing suits. All allege DRL’s patent settlement with Celgene/BMS violated antitrust and consumer protection laws by delaying generic entry until 2022 and limiting competition through 2026. Cases were consolidated; after a June 2024 order, plaintiffs filed amended complaints, and DRL moved to dismiss in October 2024. In December 2024, Insurer Plaintiffs filed Standalone Actions against DRL, Natco, Teva, and AbbVie; DRL requested leave to brief dismissal in January 2025. DRL intends to defend vigorously; liability is unascertainable, so no provision was made.

nodes.title: Other matters Internal Investigation
nodes.summary: The Company received an anonymous complaint in September 2020 alleging improper payments to healthcare professionals in Ukraine and possibly other countries, violating the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act. It disclosed the matter to the DOJ, SEC, and Securities Exchange Board of India, and engaged a U.S. law firm to investigate under Board committee instruction. In July 2021, the SEC subpoenaed related documents, which were provided. The Company continues engaging with the SEC and DOJ, including submissions on the initial and additional complaints and its Global Compliance Framework enhancements, while complying with listing obligations to update regulators. Investigations could lead to enforcement actions and civil or criminal sanctions, but outcomes and liabilities are not reasonably ascertainable at this time.
